question_record.context: A security incident was detected involving a possible attempt to access a Primary Refresh Token (PRT). This is concerning as PRT is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication across multiple devices and versions. Attackers can use this resource to move laterally or perform credential theft. The incident involves the host `vnevado-win11t` and a process `browsercore.exe` with the Process ID 7036 and commit timestamp 2024-06-20T09:29:49.304018Z. The activity was observed around the same time and is related to a midnight credential attack attempt.
question_record.question: In line with this activity, a Windows Sysinternals tool was renamed and then launched. Can you identify the name of the file that was used for this tool?
solution: There was a possible attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT) using the process `browsercore.exe`.
The host involved in the attempt to access the PRT is `vnevado-win10v`.
A Windows Sysinternals tool `mimikatz.exe` was renamed and launched, potentially for covert malicious use.

82.name: Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT)
82.description:
Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) has been detected. A Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 and later versions, iOS, and Android devices. It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

For more information, read the Activity profile: Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/e4aad043-a273-4f88-b65e-fdfc3996ec92/analystreport?
